parts.text: Tom embarked on a two-week-long journey across Europe.
In the first 4 days, he traveled 200 kilometers each day, despite the fact that he had to stop every 50 kilometers to refill his water bottle.
Over the next two days, he only managed to cover 30% of the distance he traveled in the first four days, even though he had a tailwind of 15 km/h.
On the seventh day, he took a break and didn't travel at all, choosing instead to explore a local museum.
During the second week, he made 300 kilometers every day, regardless of the fact that he had to change his bike's tire twice.
How many kilometers in total did Tom cover during his two-week-long journey?

parts.text: Conor lives near a beach and loves going there every day to have fun.
On a particular week, he found 30 people at the beach on the first day.
The next day, 10 more people were present at the beach than on the first day, and on the third day, the total number of people increased to twice the number that were there on the second day.
If Conor saw an average of 40 people each day the rest of the week, calculate the total number of people Conor saw at the beach that week.

parts.text: Rita hand-picks Junebugs off of her plants every summer.
On Monday, she removed 39 Junebugs and 21 caterpillars.
On both Tuesday and Wednesday, she removed twice as many Junebugs as she did on Monday.
Thursday she removed 48 and on Friday she removed 57.
What is the average number of Junebugs that she removes per day?
